title: Show the build commit in `athena --version` via build_info()
summary: Make `athena --version` print the package version, the source commit and a dirty marker from the existing `wiring::build_info()`, which setup fills from ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT and ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY. This replaces clap's default version string, which shows only the package version. There is no build.rs. A test covers the output.

defaults_applied.how: Change and tests are Rust only.
Adds a binary test and a formatting unit test; clippy and fmt must be clean.
Touches only the CLI's version string, reusing build_info().
Verifier runs the built binary with and without the build env vars.
Recovered the existing build_info() and the xtask env from the repository.

assumptions: Setup/xtask already export ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT and ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY (xtask/src/main.rs lines 250-251), so nothing there changes.
clap's `version` attribute currently shows only CARGO_PKG_VERSION; it must be replaced with a runtime string built from build_info().
Commit is shown in short form (first 7 characters) if xtask passes the full hash; the formatter handles either.
Dirty marker is shown as `, dirty`; unknown commit prints `unknown`.

acceptance_criteria.text: `athena --version` (and `-V`) prints the package version, the short source commit from build_info(), and a dirty marker when build_info().dirty is true, e.g. `athena 0.1.0 (abc1234, dirty)`. Check by building with ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234 ATHENA_BUILD_DIRTY=false and running the binary.
A build with no ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT prints `unknown` as the commit, and is marked dirty (existing build_info() semantics). Check by running a plain `cargo build -p athena-cli` binary.

The text comes from wiring::build_info() (a small formatting function there or in lib.rs, wired into the clap `version` attribute); no build.rs is added, and build_info()'s existing environment handling is unchanged.

A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/binary.rs runs `athena --version` and asserts the output contains the package version and either a hex commit or `unknown`; a unit test covers the formatting for clean, dirty and unknown cases. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
No new non-Rust files; no governance files change.

out_of_scope: Adding a build.rs or the vergen crate
Changing what is recorded in job records
departures: Smaller than the reference: the change is a few lines in the CLI, and build_info() and the xtask env already exist. Cost and time are lowered a little.
